business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Federal_State. Common law governs at the federal level and in British Columbia; Quebec retains a civil-law tradition for private law. BC corporate law is governed by the Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, as amended.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA, effective July 1, 2020) — Chapter 14 Investment and Chapter 20 Digital Trade
Canada–United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended by the Fifth Protocol (2008) — DTAA relevant to U.S. parent ownership and the ULC pass-through structure
Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (in force April 1, 2021)
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied since September 21, 2017)
Canada–China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (in force October 1, 2014)
Canada–Hong Kong Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (in force September 6, 2016)
Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York Convention, 1958) — applicable to cross-border publishing disputes

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Governing AML/CFT and UBO statutes: (i) Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, administered by FINTRAC; (ii) Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, ss 47, 51 and 111 respecting registered office, director records and the central securities register; (iii) Land Owner Transparency Act, SBC 2019, c 23, requiring transparency reports for land-owning BC legal persons (not applicable to a non-land-owning digital publishing ULC but included in the compliance framework); (iv) Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 21.1, establishing the federal beneficial-ownership transparency model which serves as the benchmark standard for provincial registries; (v) Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1 and Part XII.2 (terrorist financing and money laundering offences); (vi) United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 45, Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c 21 (sanctions implementation); (vii) FINTRAC guidance on ultimate beneficial ownership identification and politically exposed persons.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against: (i) the FINTRAC framework for domestic PEPs, foreign PEPs and heads of international organizations, including senior-management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring for any PEP or close associate; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List implemented under the United Nations Act; (iii) Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (iv) terrorism-financing designations under Part II.1 of the Criminal Code; (v) the U.S. OFAC SDN List and sectoral sanctions, which are mandatory given the USD-denominated Steam and PlayStation payout rails; and (vi) adverse-media, negative-news and corporate-integrity checks. All screening results, source documentation and date-of-check stamps must be preserved in the customer due diligence file and refreshed at least annually or upon any change in beneficial ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Government of British Columbia)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A BC corporate name must be expressed in English or French, or a combination, using Roman-alphabet letters and may include Arabic numerals and limited punctuation. The statutory legal element for an unlimited liability company must be exactly one of: 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée', or 'S.R.I.'. Non-Latin scripts are not registrable; no official cross-script transliteration doctrine applies. The distinctive element must not be identical or too similar to an existing reserved or registered name and must not be calculated to mislead.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Institute (when implying an academic or professional body)
Engineering (requires consent of the professional engineering regulator)
British Columbia or BC (when implying official governmental connection)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the BC Registrar of Companies issues a refusal notice citing the grounds of non-distinctiveness, misleading character or prohibited token usage. The applicant may, within 30 days of refusal, file a written Name Review Request through BC Registries customer support or by correspondence to the Registrar of Companies, BC Ministry of Finance, Victoria, British Columbia, including evidence of consent from the relevant regulator or existing name-holder, legal arguments on distinctiveness, and any trademark evidence. The Registrar will re-examine the name on the statutory criteria. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may file a new Name Reservation Request with an alternative name or apply to the British Columbia Supreme Court for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c 241. After incorporation, third-party challenges to a confusingly similar name proceed under sections 91 to 94 of the Business Corporations Act, with decisions of the Registrar reviewable by the Supreme Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as the sole statutory registered office. A BC ULC must at all times maintain a registered office in British Columbia that is a physical street address capable of accepting service of process and lawful inspection demands. A serviced or virtual office is acceptable only if it comprises a genuine physical street address in BC, is staffed during normal business hours for service acceptance and record custody, and is approved in practice by the Registrar of Companies. For a low-risk digital video-game publishing vehicle, operational personnel may work remotely, but the registered office and statutory records must remain physically accessible in BC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: under 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a standard-risk-tier digital publishing ULC. The likelihood increases materially if FINTRAC reporting thresholds are triggered, sanctions screening hits occur, PEP associations arise, or the company is flagged for insufficient commercial substance under Canadian income tax audit criteria. The Registrar and competent authorities hold statutory inspection powers over corporate records even where no physical inspection occurs.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57; sections 2, 10, 11, 52, 98, 126, 161, and 191
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia; online filing through Corporate Online at corporateonline.gov.bc.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles filed under the BCBCA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow requirement. The BC Unlimited Liability Corporation may be incorporated without paid-up capital; shares may be issued for consideration determined by the directors, subject to section 124 of the BCBCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the share subscription set out in the Incorporation Application is accepted and the initial shares are issued to the subscribers. RESOLVED that the registered office and records office are established at the address stated in the Notice of Articles. RESOLVED that the sole first director continues in office. RESOLVED that the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary-Treasurer, and Chief Financial Officer. RESOLVED that banking accounts be opened with the corporate bank, and the officers are authorized to execute banking resolutions and signatories. RESOLVED that any director or officer is authorized to execute all documents and filings necessary to complete statutory incorporation and regulatory registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry, Corporate Online name request portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search through Corporate Online or a licensed BC corporate registry agent. Submit a name reservation request for the proposed ULC name. Include the corporate name ending in 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', or the French equivalent. The reservation is valid for 56 days and may be renewed once for an additional 56 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, request an administrative review by the BC Registrar, amend the name to include consent letters from any conflicting name holders, or submit a new name reservation application with a distinctive element.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator or authorized agent; ultimately filed with BC Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles. Specify the name, registered office address, records office address, first directors, authorized share structure, and any special rights or restrictions attached to shares. For the ULC, the liability of shareholders is unlimited by virtue of section 51.1 of the BCBCA; a statement to that effect is recorded in the Notice of Articles.
required_dossiers: Consent of first directors to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar objects to the share structure or director consents, amend the defective schedule and refile through Corporate Online; the priority date will follow the resubmission unless the initial application retains a valid filing number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Statutory Filing and Pay Registry Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry via Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to Corporate Online with a registered BC Registry account, select 'File an Incorporation Application', attach the completed Notice of Articles and mandatory consents, and pay the statutory filing fee by credit card or authorized payment method. After submission, the system generates a filing acknowledgment and the application enters statutory review.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, cure the discrepancy identified in the electronic letter, resubmit the corrected filing within the specified deadline, and contact the Registrar's support line if the filing number is at risk of expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and Maintain Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation and an endorsed Notice of Articles. The company must maintain a central securities register, directors' register, and records office at the registered office or another BC location, and must ensure the Notice of Articles is available for inspection.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond the statutory service standard, request a status inquiry via Corporate Online; if the records office is queried, file a Notice of Change of Registered or Records Office within 14 days after the change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Corporate Governance Instruments and Appoint Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or use unanimous written resolutions. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution approving share issuance, registered office, officers, banking authorities, and any delegation powers. Prepare a written resolution record, maintain the corporate minute book, and issue share certificates to initial shareholders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If irregularities are found in the directors' or officers' appointments, ratify the appointment by subsequent unanimous written resolution and file the corrected resolutions in the minute book; no registry filing is required for officer changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Canada Revenue Agency and Provincial Tax Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; BC Provincial Sales Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a CRA Business Number immediately after incorporation. Register for GST/HST using the CRA's Business Registration Online or by completing RC1. If the ULC will have employees, register for payroll deductions and open a BC corporate income tax account. If the company is taxable in BC, register for the Provincial Sales Tax account with the BC Ministry of Finance.
required_dossiers: Federal incorporation or business number request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the account application due to missing entity particulars, correct the inconsistent jurisdiction or entity type, ensure the legal name matches the Registry, and resubmit the application under the same Business Number.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — digital PC and console software publishing through online stores does not require an industrial or manufacturing operating permit in British Columbia

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, British Columbia
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the venture has no physical manufacturing, no effluent discharge, no waste generation, and no land disturbance; digital store publishing does not trigger a full EIA or registration under the Environmental Assessment Act
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to purely digital operations; if a segregated server facility is later established, applicable BC O.Reg. 63/2016 and the Environmental Quality Act emission limits for electronic equipment cooling and backup generators would apply

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: WorkSafeBC registration and occupational health and safety compliance are required if the company has employees in BC. A municipal business license may be required by the local jurisdiction for the registered office or any physical premises. Fire safety, structural load, and evacuation clearances are limited to ordinary office occupancy and are confirmed through the applicable municipal building occupancy permit; no special civil defense permit is required for a software publishing undertaking.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - My Business Account and GST/HST NETFILE portal at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html for federal income tax and GST/HST; BC Ministry of Finance - eTaxBC portal at etaxbc.gov.bc.ca for provincial sales tax (PST) registration and returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the ULC under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act via BC Corporate Online to obtain the incorporation number. Step 2: Apply to CRA using Business Registration Online (BRO) for the 9-digit Business Number (BN), which is the statutory TIN; the GST/HST account (RT program account) is the VAT registration identifier. Step 3: Mandatory GST/HST registration under subsection 240(1) of the Excise Tax Act applies once taxable supplies made in Canada exceed CAD 30,000; voluntary registration is advisable to claim input tax credits on Steam/PlayStation commissions, hosting and payment processing fees. Step 4: Register for BC PST through eTaxBC under Part 9 of the Provincial Sales Tax Act if the ULC makes taxable sales of digital goods or digital services to BC consumers; there is no small-supplier exemption and PST on digital products is effective from 1 July 2024. Step 5: For a foreign-owned ULC, file an Income Tax Act section 216 election (non-resident corporation electing Part I taxation) with CRA when central management and control is exercised outside Canada, thereby being taxed on net Canadian-source business income instead of gross Part XIII withholding on royalty or dividend payments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the BC ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation under Part I of the Income Tax Act and is by default subject to entity-level corporate income tax in Canada on worldwide income, but its unlimited-liability hybrid design qualifies it as a pass-through eligible entity for foreign tax purposes, enabling a US parent to check-the-box the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership for US federal income tax while Canadian domestic enforcement continues to treat it as an entity-level taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) US Treasury Regulation 301.7701-3 check-the-box election: permitted because a BC ULC is not a per se corporation under US concepts, so a wholly owned ULC may be treated as a disregarded entity and a multi-owned ULC as a partnership. 2) Income Tax Act section 216 election: a non-resident corporation may elect to file under Part I and be taxed on net Canadian-source business income, avoiding gross 25% Part XIII withholding. 3) Excise Tax Act subsection 240(1) voluntary registration: a small-supplier exporter may elect registration to recover input tax credits on platform costs while zero-rating export turnover. 4) Excise Tax Act subsection 273(1) business acquisition election: allows acquisition of an existing video game catalogue on a tax-deferred basis. 5) BC has no check-the-box style election for PST; however, eTaxBC allows the registrant to elect monthly, quarterly or annual PST filing frequencies based on projected taxable sales volume.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) administered by CRA, plus a separate British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) administered by the BC Ministry of Finance; BC does not participate in the HST, so the combined consumer rate in BC is 12% (5% GST + 7% PST) applied and reported as two distinct taxes on digital game downloads.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in annual taxable supplies made in Canada (small-supplier threshold under Excise Tax Act subsection 148(1)); BC PST: no monetary threshold - a vendor must register through eTaxBC before making any taxable supply of digital goods or digital services to BC consumers, with the digital product PST extension effective 1 July 2024.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, digital stamping, or pre-clearance e-invoice API regime. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE) and are due within one month after the reporting period end. Computer-generated invoices are acceptable and no national clearing house exists. BC PST returns are filed through eTaxBC; invoices must show the vendor PST registration number and comply with Provincial Sales Tax Act record retention rules. Steam and PlayStation payout rails do not require any Canadian tax clearance step; Valve and Sony Interactive Entertainment provide sales and remittance reports that serve as the contractual evidence base for GST/PST self-assessment and settlement reconciliation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Digital video games supplied through Steam and PlayStation storefronts to non-resident customers qualify for a 0% GST/HST rate as supplies of services made to non-resident persons under section 9 of Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, provided the ULC is registered and maintains billing address, IP geolocation and storefront jurisdiction evidence demonstrating each recipient is outside Canada. Sales to Canadian residents are taxable at 5% GST plus 7% BC PST where the purchaser is in BC. BC PST export exemption applies where the digital good is not used in BC; Steam/PlayStation settlements representing export revenue are excluded from PST, and input tax credits on platform fees remain recoverable to the extent attributable to zero-rated export supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Statutory core bundle for physical exports: CRA Form B13A (Customs Export Declaration), transport document (Bill of Lading or Air Waybill), and inward remittance certificate evidencing FX repatriation
Digital delivery adaptation: Steamworks publisher agreement and monthly Steam payout and settlement reports from Valve Corporation
PlayStation Store publisher agreement and monthly royalty and sales reports from Sony Interactive Entertainment
Commercial invoices per reporting period showing game title, unit volumes, platform commission and net settlement amounts
Non-resident customer evidence: storefront billing country codes, IP geolocation logs and payment card country codes
Inward remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103 advices or bank FX conversion statements showing funds received into the ULC Canadian bank account
GST/HST return and zero-rated supplies reconciliation schedule (GST34 line 105) matched to the platform sales reports
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where the CRA recharacterises a purported export supply as a supply to a Canadian resident, it assesses 5% GST on the gross settlement, denies the attributable input tax credits, and imposes interest and arrears assessments. The standard reassessment window is 4 years, extended to 10 years for misrepresentation or fraud (Excise Tax Act subsections 298(1) and 298(3)). False zero-rating claims attract a gross-negligence penalty of 20% of the relevant net tax under section 285.1, and criminal evasion proceedings under section 327.1 carry fines up to CAD 200,000 and/or up to 2 years imprisonment on summary conviction, and fines up to CAD 2,000,000 and/or up to 5 years imprisonment on indictment. Under the BC Provincial Sales Tax Act, failure to collect or remit PST results in a 25% penalty plus interest under the Tax Administration Act; CRA and BC audit programs include data matching with digital platform operators, so retrospective clawbacks are probable where the non-residency or out-of-province use evidence trail is incomplete.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); fiscal agent for the Government of Canada's Exchange Fund Account under the Department of Finance Canada; prudential regulation of banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions. Canada has no separate foreign-exchange control administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Both capital and current accounts are fully convertible; the Canadian dollar floats freely. No prior approval is required for capital injection, dividends, royalties, interest, or liquidation remittances. Profit remittance is constrained only by Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% statutory, treaty-reduced) and standard bank documentation. A BC ULC is a Canadian-resident corporation for Canadian tax purposes even when a U.S. parent elects check-the-box flow-through treatment; the election does not create Canadian pass-through status.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender obligation at federal or provincial level. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio; 0% of foreign currency export receipts must be converted. Digital store proceeds are treated as export of services for balance-of-payments and income tax purposes and may be retained in USD or converted at the ULC's discretion. Reporting obligations remain: annual CRA T1135 for specified foreign property above CAD 100,000; FINTRAC reports for cross-border electronic fund transfers at or above CAD 10,000; and translation to CAD for Canadian tax return purposes using the Bank of Canada exchange rate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report Form (British Columbia Business Corporations Act, s. 383)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry (BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation; if the ULC elected a fiscal year end with notice, within 60 days after that fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 40 after due date; continued default may lead to administrative dissolution without further notice and reinstatement costs, liabilities, and potential loss of legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notice of Directors and Registered Address Confirmation (embedded in Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry (via Annual Report submission)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same 60-day anniversary window as Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or overdue director information may attract administrative penalties, and the registrar may refuse to issue compliance certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private BC ULC is not subject to a mandatory statutory audit unless a shareholder holding at least 10% of the eligible shares makes a written demand, or the entity is a public company, a controlled entity under a regulatory statute, or articles of association require an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS, ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises), or US GAAP as acceptable for Canadian tax reporting; for a BC private ULC, ASPE is the most common choice unless shareholder agreements or distribution agreements require IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Directors and shareholders must be listed in the Annual Report; while BC does not maintain a public beneficial ownership registry, the ULC must keep an internal Register of Individuals with Significant Control and update it continually. The annual confirmation verifies the director list and registered office, and any UBO changes must be reflected in the corporate records and be available for inspection by law enforcement or tax authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 5,000 for a private ULC with low transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction: federal rate reduced to 9% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; BC small business rate reduced to 2% on same threshold. Additional incentives include Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credits for qualifying software R&D, and the Digital Media Tax Credit (BC) for eligible interactive digital media products.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically via CRA's e-file (for tax preparers) or NETFILE (for corporations) at canada.ca
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., if year-end is December 31, deadline is June 30 of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from all sources, including sales of video games via digital platforms (Steam, PlayStation Store) and any ancillary income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross revenue in Canadian dollars; convert foreign currency using the Bank of Canada annual average exchange rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for cost of goods sold, including platform fees (e.g., Valve's 30% commission), royalties paid to third-party IP holders, and direct production costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all deductions are supported by invoices and contracts; allocate costs on a reasonable basis if mixed with other activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying all deductions, including capital cost allowance (CCA) on equipment and intangible assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a ULC, compute taxable income as per Part I of the Income Tax Act; consider any adjustments for non-deductible expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax payable before credits, calculated at the applicable rate (15% general or 9% small business on eligible income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the small business deduction only if the corporation is a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) and meets the ownership criteria.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial tax payable to British Columbia, calculated at 12% general rate or 2% small business rate on eligible income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: BC provincial tax is based on taxable income allocated to BC; use the BC corporate tax return (T2 BC) if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax credits claimed, including SR&ED investment tax credits, digital media tax credits, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach supporting schedules (e.g., T2SCH31 for SR&ED) and ensure eligibility for non-resident-owned ULCs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months (maximum 17%). Late payment interest: daily compound interest at the prescribed rate (currently 8% for corporations). Additional penalties for repeated failures or gross negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, unless reduced by a tax treaty)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a tax treaty (e.g., Canada-US), the non-resident shareholder must provide the payer with a completed Form NR-301 (for US residents) or NR-302 (for other countries) along with a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority. The form must be submitted before the dividend payment to allow the payer to withhold at the reduced rate. If not provided, the statutory 25% rate applies, and the non-resident may file a refund claim with the CRA using Form NR-7.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rates (Canada-US): 10% for royalties (including software royalties) and 10% for interest, but interest may be exempt if paid to a US resident at arm's length and not participating in the payer's business. For other countries, rates vary; e.g., Canada-UK treaty provides 10% for royalties and 10% for interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate transactions with non-residents in a fiscal year (triggering mandatory Local File and Master File preparation under CRA guidelines)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) like the UAE, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under Section 245 of the Income Tax Act applies to transactions lacking economic substance. For treaty benefits, the Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clause in the Canada-US treaty requires the entity to have substantive business operations and not be a conduit. A ULC must demonstrate real economic activity (e.g., employees, office, decision-making) to avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting revenue from digital sales, inflating deductions, or failing to report foreign income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Section 239 of the Income Tax Act: fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil penalties: 50% of the understated tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes under Section 227.1 if they failed to withhold or remit amounts. Civil restitution, travel bans, and potential imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a passive holding entity with no real employees, assets, or business activities in Canada, while claiming treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reassessment of income, and application of GAAR to recharacterize transactions. Penalties up to 25% of the tax avoided.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in the sham arrangement. Personal assets may be seized, and travel restrictions imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for platform fees, royalties, or services that deviate from arm's length, resulting in profit shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties of 10% of the net adjustment (if the adjustment exceeds the lesser of 10% of gross revenue or CAD 5 million), and interest on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they signed false or misleading transfer pricing documentation. Civil penalties and potential criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the T2 filing deadline or failing to remit payroll source deductions (if any employees)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty of 5% plus 1% per month (max 17%), late remittance penalty of 10% of the amount, and interest on unpaid amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unremitted source deductions under Section 227.1. The CRA can issue a director's liability assessment and pursue personal assets.
